item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, reduce only the pointwise-loss coefficient from 0.2 to 0.1, retaining BPR and valid-position averaging. Weaker absolute-score calibration may let pairwise ranking better match HR@10 without discarding its stabilizing effect. Preserve the GRU, embeddings, readout, scoring, sampling, optimizer and training schedule; train one model per category.","1":"Across all four datasets, change only the causal readout blend from 0.8*h_t+0.2*m_t to 0.9*h_t+0.1*m_t, retaining the three-interaction pooling half-life. This tests whether a smaller broader-interest contribution improves next-item specificity. Exclude padding and future states, retain final-real-position inference, and synchronize the predictor writer. Preserve all other settings and one model per category.","2":"Across all four datasets, replace tied unit-normalized item vectors with r_i*normalize(v_i), where r_i=1+0.1*tanh(a_i) and each jointly trained a_i starts at zero. A bounded item-specific radius may capture differences in predictive strength while retaining the incumbent angular representation and initial behavior. Keep padding zero, dimensions, GRU, readout, dot-product scoring, loss and optimizer fixed. Save radii in the single category checkpoint and update predictor loading.","3":"Across all four datasets, construct a fixed training-frequency feature: compute each item's percentile q_i among positive training-item counts and multiply its history input embedding by 0.95+0.10*q_i. This mildly emphasizes better-supported observations without adding a separate scorer. Use only supplied training interactions, keep padding zero and candidate embeddings unchanged, and persist the feature lookup for identical inference. Preserve learned embedding design, GRU topology, readout, loss, optimizer and one model per category."}
